scenes.title: A chat bot that answers, researches and plans

cues.text: The assistant is a chat bot on Slack and Discord.
It answers questions about your code and your Symphony install.
It researches a topic, and it plans work as tickets.
A person confirms a plan before any ticket exists.
It runs as one deployment that dials out to Slack and Discord, so it needs no public URL.
cues.say: It runs as one deployment that dials out to Slack and Discord, so it needs no public U R L.

cues.text: Mention it in an allowed channel, send it a direct message, or reply in its thread.
A plain question goes to the assistant role.
It posts Working on it at once, then edits that message as the answer streams.
Start with research, and the researcher digs through the code, the tracker and the web.
Start with plan, and the planner turns a goal into tickets.
Each mode is a team role with its own model.
A follow-up without a mode word keeps the thread's role.
The agents read your repositories at origin main.
A code citation names the repository, the path and the line.
The assistant turns it into a link to GitHub, at the commit the agent read.
The agent can read, grep, glob and search the web.
Symphony status shows tickets, sessions, the merger queue and recent failures.
Tracker search looks up tickets in Linear or GitHub.
It cannot run commands, change files, push, comment, or move a ticket.
Its environment holds no chat, tracker or GitHub App credential.

scenes.title: A plan waits for a person's click

cues.text: The planner never creates tickets. It calls propose tickets.
The assistant posts the plan with three buttons.
Create puts the tickets in Backlog, with a repository label.
Create and start uses the first active state and the symphony label, so the daemon picks them up.
Dismiss creates nothing.
Only a person mapped in notify.users can click.
cues.say: Only a person mapped in notify users can click.

cues.text: Anyone else gets a private answer, and nothing is created.
The audit actor is that person's GitHub login.

scenes.title: Safe to click twice, with real blocking links

cues.text: A claim key lets one click work at a time.
A second click meanwhile hears that the tickets are being created.
Each created ticket is recorded by its key.
So a double click, or a retry after a failure, never creates a ticket twice.
Parents and blockers come first, and a child becomes a sub-issue.
Each blocked-by becomes a real blocking relation in the tracker.
cues.say: Each blocked by becomes a real blocking relation in the tracker.

cues.text: If the tracker refuses a link, the assistant says so in a comment on the ticket.
The audit log records the creation, with the login and the identifiers.

scenes.title: Each thread is an assist session

cues.text: Each chat thread is an assist session, and Tern's Sessions view lists it.
The row shows the mode, the transport, the channel and the thread.
Open it to follow the turn live.
A steer reaches the running turn.
A follow-up becomes the thread's next question, and the answer goes to the chat.
At most three turns run at once. After 30 idle minutes, the session ends.
cues.say: At most three turns run at once. After thirty idle minutes, the session ends.

scenes.title: The Slack app token and the Discord intent

cues.text: The assistant reuses the bots of the notifications step.
On Slack, turn on Socket Mode, and make an app-level token with connections write.
On Discord, turn on the Message Content intent of the bot.
Then run symphony setup assistant, with the channels and the repositories.
The app token comes from standard input or a hidden prompt.
The API checks both Slack tokens, and the intent on Discord.
Then it publishes the settings in WORKFLOW and restarts the assistant.
cues.say: Then it publishes the settings in the workflow, and restarts the assistant.

cues.text: In Tern, the same form is the Assistant step of Setup.
The mocked certification tested the assistant end to end.
On Slack, the envelope was acked in three milliseconds.
The answer, with its code citation, came after about ten seconds.
A mapped click created three tickets in Linear in half a second, with a blocking relation.
An unmapped click was refused, and a double click created nothing.
On Discord, with the GitHub tracker, the same flow passed.
Every check passed.
